newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Lifeless" French grain market mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: "Lifeless" French grain market mostly weaker.

text.p: French wheat and maize prices drifted in an uninspiring start to the week while barley was a touch firmer at Dunkirk, traders said on Monday.
Wheat, already searching around in vain for support from exports on Friday, took a further knock from thin domestic and European demand, they said.
"The market is lifeless," a local operator said, adding there were few positions left uncovered from end-users inside the European Union.
Rouen-delivered wheat for February found bidders at 850 francs a tonne at public silos, and 852.50 francs at private ones, compared with 855 francs at both types on Friday.
First-hand sellers were sticking to their previous asking levels, however, at 860 francs in Rouen and 855 francs in Dunkirk, brokers said.
May fob barge Matif wheat futures were bid at 888 francs a tonne and offered at 889 francs a tonne but there was no trade for any contract month.

Cash barley was mixed, with bids of 850 francs unchanged at Rouen, while Dunkirk -- the main export outlet for large-vessel business such as recent sales to Saudi Arabia -- saw bids around 10 francs higher than Friday's levels for February and March.
Barley had traded on Friday at 865 francs and then 860 francs, they said.
As in previous days, maize was depressed in the southwest by slack Atlantic export demand.
The few buyers at Bordeaux were looking to pay 835 francs a tonne for delivered material while maize at La Pallice was five francs lower.
On the Rhine, maize was unchanged at 875 francs per tonne, traders said.
French cash grain prices exclude carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne, which must be added to every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question.
For example, the carrying charge supplement for second-half February is 50.90 francs a tonne.
